The suite is green (BUILD SUCCESS, the single acceptance test passes; `AcceptanceBase`/`AuditLogCapture` are support classes, not test cases).

## Summary

The effective registration date (supplied or defaulted to server date) now rolls forward off weekends to the next Monday, and everything derived from it follows automatically.

Changes, kept small and low-impact:

1. **`BuildOwner.java`** — resolves the effective date (request value or `LocalDate.now()`), and if it lands on Saturday/Sunday rolls it to the next Monday before storing it on the owner. Because the membership number's year segment (`OwnerMapper`) reads `owner.getRegistrationDate().getYear()`, it now uses the adjusted date with no change needed there.

2. **`owners.POST.yml`** — moved `ensureDailyLimit` to run *after* `build`, so the limit check sees the already-adjusted owner rather than needing its own copy of the date logic.

3. **`EnsureDailyLimit.java`** — now counts existing owners against the built owner's adjusted `registrationDate` (`@Val Owner`) instead of the raw `LocalDate.now()`, so the daily cap is enforced per adjusted business day.

Each edited method stays at CC ≈ 2–3 with no surrounding sibling complexity, the roll-forward logic lives in exactly one place (`BuildOwner`), and no new class or duplicate helper was introduced — three files touched total.
